# UK Website — Build Guide
## Subniche: British Home Interior Styling & Room Makeovers

---

## Stack

- **Framework**: Astro (outputs static HTML — fastest possible load speed)
- **Hosting**: Hostinger
- **Domain**: `.co.uk` TLD (e.g. `britishhomeinterior.co.uk`)
- **Language**: `en-GB` (British English — critical for UK Pinterest targeting)

---

## Project Structure

```
britishhomeinterior.co.uk/
├── public/
│   ├── robots.txt
│   ├── sitemap.xml          ← auto-generated by Astro
│   └── favicon.ico
├── src/
│   ├── layouts/
│   │   └── BlogPost.astro   ← main layout used by every post
│   ├── pages/
│   │   ├── index.astro      ← homepage
│   │   ├── blog/
│   │   │   └── [slug].astro ← dynamic blog post route
│   │   └── about.astro
│   ├── components/
│   │   ├── Header.astro
│   │   ├── Footer.astro
│   │   ├── SEO.astro        ← all meta tags go here
│   │   └── FAQ.astro        ← reusable FAQ component with schema
│   └── content/
│       └── blog/            ← your .md or .mdx post files go here
├── astro.config.mjs
└── package.json
```

---

## Astro Config

```js
// astro.config.mjs
import { defineConfig } from 'astro/config';
import sitemap from '@astrojs/sitemap';

export default defineConfig({
  site: 'https://britishhomeinterior.co.uk',
  integrations: [
    sitemap(),
  ],
});
```

---

## SEO Component — Every Meta Tag You Need

```astro
---
// src/components/SEO.astro
const {
  title,
  description,
  slug,
  image,
  datePublished,
  dateModified,
  authorName = "Your Name",
} = Astro.props;

const siteUrl = "https://britishhomeinterior.co.uk";
const fullUrl = `${siteUrl}/blog/${slug}`;
const fullImage = `${siteUrl}${image}`;
---

<!-- Primary Meta Tags -->
<title>{title}</title>
<meta name="description" content={description} />
<meta name="robots" content="index, follow" />
<link rel="canonical" href={fullUrl} />
<html lang="en-GB" />

<!-- Open Graph — Pinterest reads these for Rich Pins -->
<meta property="og:type" content="article" />
<meta property="og:title" content={title} />
<meta property="og:description" content={description} />
<meta property="og:url" content={fullUrl} />
<meta property="og:image" content={fullImage} />
<meta property="og:image:width" content="1200" />
<meta property="og:image:height" content="630" />
<meta property="og:locale" content="en_GB" />
<meta property="og:site_name" content="British Home Interior" />

<!-- Twitter Card -->
<meta name="twitter:card" content="summary_large_image" />
<meta name="twitter:title" content={title} />
<meta name="twitter:description" content={description} />
<meta name="twitter:image" content={fullImage} />

<!-- Article Meta -->
<meta property="article:published_time" content={datePublished} />
<meta property="article:modified_time" content={dateModified} />
<meta property="article:author" content={authorName} />

<!-- Article Schema (JSON-LD) -->
<script type="application/ld+json">
{JSON.stringify({
  "@context": "https://schema.org",
  "@type": "Article",
  "headline": title,
  "description": description,
  "image": fullImage,
  "datePublished": datePublished,
  "dateModified": dateModified,
  "author": {
    "@type": "Person",
    "name": authorName,
    "url": `${siteUrl}/about`
  },
  "publisher": {
    "@type": "Organization",
    "name": "British Home Interior",
    "logo": {
      "@type": "ImageObject",
      "url": `${siteUrl}/logo.png`
    }
  },
  "mainEntityOfPage": {
    "@type": "WebPage",
    "@id": fullUrl
  }
})}
</script>
```

## FAQ Component — Boosts AI Citation Rate by 340%

```astro
---
// src/components/FAQ.astro
const { questions } = Astro.props;
// questions = [{ q: "Question?", a: "Answer under 60 words." }]
---

<section class="faq-section">
  <h2>Frequently Asked Questions</h2>

  {questions.map((item) => (
    <div class="faq-item">
      <h3>{item.q}</h3>
      <p>{item.a}</p>
    </div>
  ))}
</section>

<!-- FAQPage Schema -->
<script type="application/ld+json">
{JSON.stringify({
  "@context": "https://schema.org",
  "@type": "FAQPage",
  "mainEntity": questions.map((item) => ({
    "@type": "Question",
    "name": item.q,
    "acceptedAnswer": {
      "@type": "Answer",
      "text": item.a
    }
  }))
})}
</script>
```

**How to use in any blog post:**
```astro
<FAQ questions={[
  { q: "What are the best living room ideas for a UK home?", a: "Cottagecore, maximalist layering, and dark moody palettes are the top trends for British living rooms in 2026. Focus on cosy textures — linen, velvet, and rattan work particularly well in UK interiors." },
  { q: "How do I style a small flat in the UK on a budget?", a: "Use mirrors to add depth, shop Dunelm and Next Home for affordable statement pieces, and focus on one feature wall. A budget room makeover in the UK is very achievable under £200." }
]} />
```

## Blog Post Layout

```astro
---
// src/layouts/BlogPost.astro
const {
  title,
  description,
  slug,
  image,
  datePublished,
  dateModified,
} = Astro.props;
---

<html lang="en-GB">
  <head>
    <meta charset="UTF-8" />
    <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0" />
    <SEO
      title={title}
      description={description}
      slug={slug}
      image={image}
      datePublished={datePublished}
      dateModified={dateModified}
    />
  </head>
  <body>
    <Header />
    <main>
      <article>
        <h1>{title}</h1>
        <slot /> <!-- blog post content renders here -->
      </article>
    </main>
    <Footer />
  </body>
</html>
```

## Blog Post Frontmatter (every .md file)

```markdown
---
title: "21 Living Room Ideas UK — Cosy Styles on a Budget (2026)"
description: "Transform your British living room with these 21 cosy decorating ideas. Budget home interior inspiration for UK homes, flats, and Victorian terraces."
slug: "living-room-ideas-uk-budget"
image: "/images/living-room-ideas-uk.jpg"
datePublished: "2026-01-15"
dateModified: "2026-01-15"
author: "Your Name"
tags: ["living room ideas UK", "home interior UK", "budget home decor", "British interior"]
---

## TL;DR
- 21 cosy living room ideas for UK homes and flats
- All styles achievable under £200
- Includes cottagecore, maximalist, and dark moody options

[rest of post content...]
```

> **Critical**: Use British English spelling in ALL content — colour, cosy, organise, favourite, flat, mum, grey, centre. This signals UK relevance to both Pinterest and Google.

## Mobile-First CSS

```css
/* Base mobile styles — applied first */
body {
  font-family: system-ui, sans-serif;
  font-size: 18px;
  line-height: 1.7;
  color: #1a1a1a;
  background: #ffffff;
  margin: 0;
  padding: 0;
}

/* Single column layout */
main {
  max-width: 720px;
  margin: 0 auto;
  padding: 0 20px;
}

/* Short paragraphs, plenty of white space */
p {
  margin-bottom: 1.5rem;
}

/* Subheading every 200-300 words */
h2 {
  font-size: 1.6rem;
  margin-top: 2.5rem;
  margin-bottom: 1rem;
}

h3 {
  font-size: 1.3rem;
  margin-top: 2rem;
}

/* Images fill container */
img {
  width: 100%;
  height: auto;
  display: block;
  border-radius: 8px;
}

/* Desktop — wider content */
@media (min-width: 768px) {
  main {
    max-width: 800px;
    padding: 0 40px;
  }
}
```

## Pinterest Rich Pins Setup

After your site is live, verify your domain with Pinterest to enable Rich Pins:

1. Go to Pinterest → Settings → Claim → Claim Website
2. Add the verification meta tag Pinterest gives you inside your `<head>`
3. Go to: `https://developers.pinterest.com/tools/url-debugger/`
4. Enter any blog post URL and click "Validate"
5. Rich Pins will be approved within 24 hours

Rich Pins automatically pull your `og:title`, `og:description`, and `og:image` onto every pin — no manual entry needed.

## Country Targeting Checklist

- [ ] Domain is `.co.uk`
- [ ] `lang="en-GB"` on `<html>` tag
- [ ] `og:locale` set to `en_GB`
- [ ] All prices shown in **GBP (£)**
- [ ] British English used throughout: colour, cosy, organise, grey, flat, mum, centre
- [ ] References to UK retailers: Dunelm, John Lewis, Next Home, IKEA UK, Wayfair UK
- [ ] UK location references: Victorian terrace, British home, UK flat
- [ ] Pinterest account country set to **United Kingdom**
- [ ] Pinterest account language set to **English (UK)**

## Install Commands

```bash
# Create Astro project
npm create astro@latest britishhomeinterior

# Install sitemap integration
npx astro add sitemap

# Run locally
npm run dev

# Build for production
npm run build
```
